newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY LEAGUE-AUSTRALIAN REBELS TO FOLLOW EUROPEAN LEAD.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-AUSTRALIAN REBELS TO FOLLOW EUROPEAN LEAD.

text.p: Australia's reborn Super League
said on Monday it would follow the example of its European
counterpart and use a system of video referees for judging tries
when the breakaway rugby league competition begins next year.
The new refereeing technique was one of several innovations
Super League officials said they had planned for the game after
a court victory on Friday freed media baron Rupert Murdoch's
competition to start next year.
It comes after several rule changes were announced on Sunday
which Super League officials said were designed to make the game
faster and more attractive to spectators.
Super League matches in Australia next year will use
television replays to support the match referee on the ground in
cases where there is doubt whether a try has been properly
scored.
The video system was used by Europe's Super League, also
controlled by Murdoch, in its first season this year.
In such situations a second referee in the grandstand will
examine video replays of the incident and determine whether the
try should be awarded.
As with the European league, replays will be shown at the
same time on large video screens to spectators.
"A lot of people said it wouldn't work, but it does work and
it has been working in England," Super League football
operations manager Graham Annesley told a news conference.
Annesley also announced Super League would use a team of 29
referees and touch judges, many of them former employees of the
Australian Rugby League (ARL). The game's traditional governing
body, the ARL has been engaged in a bitter battle with Murdoch
for control of the sport for almost two years.
Many of those referees and touch judges were left unemployed
after a court ruling last March banned Super League until 2000.
That decision was overturned in Friday's appeal ruling.
